entries.title: Light, energy and invariant mass
entries.summary: Light has measurable energy and momentum. A nonzero invariant photon rest mass is a separate hypothesis, not a consequence of radiation pressure or gravity.

related.label: Conservative mode coupling and massive-vector sector

entries.keywords: Photons have mass. E² = C²p² + Eₘ²;  v_g/C = √(1−g²),  g = Eₘ/E

entries.title: One progression, different clock readings
entries.summary: The proposed universal progression T is a research choice. Different measured clock counts must be explained; identical progression does not establish a detectable absolute clock.
entries.keywords: Time is constant. N_A = ν_A T; N_B = ν_B T; N_SR = ν_A T√(1−β²)

entries.title: Distinguishing energy loss from slowing
entries.summary: Energy, frequency and group speed are distinct. A fixed-gap drag model permits energy loss with very little speed change, and the zero-gap limit does not slow at all.
entries.keywords: Light slows down over time. p = p₀ exp(−γT); E = √(p²+g²); v_g = p/E

entries.title: Time as event ordering
entries.summary: The charter treats When as a relation between events. That ontological choice must be distinguished from measured duration and relativistic proper time.
entries.keywords: Time does not physically exist; it is the “When.” t_emit(n)=nP; t_arr(n)=nP+L/C; Δt_arr=P

entries.title: Space as measurable relations
entries.summary: Relative position, separation and geometry are measurable. The choice not to call space a material does not remove geometric laws.
entries.keywords: Space does not physically exist; it is the “Where.” d = √((x₂−x₁)²+(y₂−y₁)²)

entries.title: Physical attributes and system mass
entries.summary: Physical states carry measurable energy and momentum, but energy-equivalent mass, invariant mass and geometric extent are distinct quantities.
entries.keywords: All that physically exists at any moment occupies area and has mass at that moment. M²c⁴ = 2E₁E₂(1−cos θ)

entries.title: Geometry versus a literal fabric
entries.summary: Relativistic geometry is a successful predictive framework. Rejecting a literal fabric metaphor does not reject measured proper times, trajectories or gravity.
entries.keywords: Spacetime does not physically exist. Δτ/Δt = √(1−β²)

entries.title: Group speed and causal speed
entries.summary: A field characteristic may be faster than a slow massive packet without exceeding the local causal maximum. No controllable faster-than-light signal is demonstrated.
entries.keywords: Light is not the fastest thing in the universe. t_packet = D/v_g; t_front = D/C; Δt = D(1/v_g−1/C)

entries.title: Closing and separation rates versus causality
entries.summary: Coordinate separation rates may exceed a local light-speed benchmark; this does not imply that one body or signal travels locally faster than c.
entries.keywords: Things move apart from each other faster than causality; time, space, or spacetime cannot be physically stretched because they are not physical substances to stretch. V_sep/C = 2β; v_rel/C = 2β/(1+β²)

entries.title: Observable reach and total cosmic extent
entries.summary: A finite causal reach does not determine the total physical extent of the universe. The observable horizon is not necessarily a material wall.
entries.keywords: The size of the universe is unknown. R_reach = C T; observed fraction = min(1,(R_reach/R_domain)³)

entries.title: Modeled cosmic age and total history
entries.summary: The conventional cosmic age is an inference from a calibrated expansion history. The duration of all hypothetical physical reality is a different, unanswered question.
entries.keywords: The age of the universe is unknown. t₀ = 2 asinh(√((1−Ωm)/Ωm))/(3 H₀√(1−Ωm))

entries.title: When astronomical distances and sizes can change
entries.summary: Distance corrections are testable and can have either sign. The charter’s smaller-and-closer premise must not become an assumed correction for every object.
entries.keywords: Objects in the universe are smaller and closer than they appear. D_inferred/D = 10^(A/5); size ratio = distance ratio (fixed small angle)

entries.title: The twelve foundations
entries.summary: The twelve statements define the investigator’s research charter.
entries.keywords: Charter A declared premise is not an empirical result. Test concrete implementations against independent observations.

entries.title: C-01: emission ceiling
entries.summary: The origin of the local emission ceiling is a research objective; distinguish characteristic, group and front speeds.
entries.keywords: Light No calibrated mechanism fixes the observed ceiling. Derive a causal finite-source response with calibrated matter standards.

entries.title: Screened common-field obstruction
entries.summary: A-05c did not identify a stable joint parameter regime satisfying slowing, atomic spectra, lensing and multimessenger constraints.
entries.keywords: Fields Restricted to the investigated model family; not a general no-go theorem. Derive a revised coupling and evaluate all constraints jointly.

entries.title: Finite-source screening
entries.summary: Finite-size suppression is weaker than the local-equilibrium estimate suggests.
entries.keywords: Fields Conditional bounds and illustrative numerical results, not measured field screening. Solve finite 3D sources with shared atomic calibration.

entries.title: Early recession-distance candidate
entries.summary: Early recession-plus-slowing distance candidates encounter high-redshift size and drift tension.
entries.keywords: Cosmology Failure of these implementations does not establish an alternative distance law. Fit held-out angle, timing, flux and spectrum data with shared parameters.

entries.title: Conservative mode coupling and massive-vector sector
entries.summary: Restricted analytical and numerical demonstrations include scalar coupling, Stueckelberg/Yukawa response and atomic shifts.
entries.keywords: Light Not a measured photon rest mass or complete matter theory. Predict static range, longitudinal modes and atomic spectra with one parameter set.

entries.title: Moving atomic endpoints
entries.summary: Autonomous one-dimensional separation and moving atomic endpoints give selected spectra dominated by motion.
entries.keywords: Motion Dimensionless toy, not calibrated cosmology. Derive coupled source motion and detector response.

entries.title: Packet reach versus causal reach
entries.summary: Packet reach and causal reach differ; bounded scalar energy prevents eternal zero speed in the stated model.
entries.keywords: Light A group-velocity result does not determine the signal front. Derive stable characteristic and front behavior from the full local theory.

entries.title: Reciprocal optical maps
entries.summary: The static and axisymmetric optical audit finds a brightness-factor tension despite reciprocal maps and weak spherical defocusing.
entries.keywords: Distances No fitted cosmology or universal distance correction. Predict luminosity and angular distances with one transport model.

entries.title: C-01 shell and void control
entries.summary: The candidate mass-sourced regulator yields a wave-speed law but fails monotone aging across the shell.
entries.keywords: Domains No detected cosmic wall; Newtonian shell force and regulator response are separate. Develop a causal gap-history and recoil mechanism.

entries.title: Passive fixed-gap drag
entries.summary: For the stationary fixed-gap benchmark, modest redshift gives tiny speed change; identical stationary emission intervals are not stretched by the aging law.
entries.keywords: Light Restricted fixed-gap, stationary-endpoint result. Test a moving-endpoint or derived dynamical transport model against spectrum and timing together.

entries.title: Fixed-gap wall energy bound
entries.summary: For a gap fraction 10⁻¹⁶ and a 10% ceiling increase, the maximum retained energy fraction for nonincreasing endpoint speed is about 2.4004 × 10⁻¹⁶.
entries.keywords: Domains Necessary endpoint bound only; not a sufficient pathwise criterion. Check energy retention and continuous trajectory sign together.

entries.title: Linear-wall constant-drag conflict
entries.summary: At gap fraction 0.1 and ceiling ratio 1.2, entry monotonicity requires drag ≥ 19.89975, whereas positive-speed traversal requires drag < 3.28345.
entries.keywords: Domains This rules out the selected constant-drag control, not all environmental models. Derive and test a variable gap or history mechanism.

entries.title: Finite-capacity history coordinate
entries.summary: A selected reduced wall model adds a history coordinate with recoil, heat and wall-reaction ledgers, permitting a different crossing behavior.
entries.keywords: Light Finite capacity and emission-energy dependence prevent a universal solution. Derive microscopic dynamics with a causal receiver, not a stipulated history rate.

entries.title: Bounded flow and reversible conversion
entries.summary: Reduced controls include bounded flow, calibration, finite wall recoil and reversible local conversion.
entries.keywords: Motion Not one unified physical or observationally fitted theory. Couple the models and calibrate independent source and receiver standards.

entries.title: Contact conversion loses narrow-beam transport
entries.summary: One-arcsecond idealized aperture accepts about 1.44456 × 10⁻¹³ of converted packets in the selected contact reference.
entries.keywords: Light Conditional acceptance after conversion, not an astronomical optical depth or luminosity-distance fit. Derive forward transport, actual detection and angular diffusion.

entries.title: Continuous static-wall certificate
entries.summary: The fine interval enclosure reports an upper derivative bound −0.05341 in the rising wall and a path speed lower bound 0.81507.
entries.keywords: Domains Only the original static reduced trajectory and parameter case; not an all-frequency or astronomical proof. Independently verify intervals and extend to derived moving-wall dynamics.

entries.title: LMC geometric anchor
entries.summary: Review 6.0 reports the literature eclipsing-binary distance 49.59 kpc, statistical 0.09 and systematic 0.54 kpc.
entries.keywords: Distances Specific calibrated inference; quadrature arithmetic is not a new joint fit. Preserve raw anchor observations and recalibrate any candidate correction.

entries.title: NGC 4258 geometric anchor
entries.summary: Review 6.0 reports the literature maser distance 7.576 Mpc, statistical 0.082 and systematic 0.076 Mpc.
entries.keywords: Distances No universal downward rescaling is inferred. Recover the maser geometry with shared calibrated parameters.

entries.title: Finite-range forward-transfer obstruction
entries.summary: Large gap conversion has a nonzero forward-transfer floor; the near-degenerate example gives cone fraction about 0.8844 and mean retained energy 0.9999989997.
entries.keywords: Light Born-level selected cases; near-degenerate transfer is minute and repeated scattering is unsolved. Derive material structure factors, cumulative angular diffusion and optical depth.

entries.title: Collinear phase-matched reservoir
entries.summary: A selected coherent reservoir mode permits collinear phase-matched conversion, while finite-cell coupling has detuning and reverse-transition controls.
entries.keywords: Light Coherence, material structure and physical rates are not derived or calibrated. Derive a causal spatial reservoir and its spectral density.

entries.title: Escape-assisted population criterion
entries.summary: For the resonant selected-mode Markov model, κ ≥ 4G ensures nondecreasing total converted population.
entries.keywords: Light Not a theorem of continuous slowing of individual photons; no incoming reservoir excitation assumed. Derive a multimode reservoir with reverse channels and detector calibration.

entries.title: Escape analytical-versus-ODE comparison
entries.summary: Six escape ratios 0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 at G=0.04 agree to maximum sampled absolute difference 1.54 × 10⁻¹³ after solver refinement.
entries.keywords: Light Reported source comparison, not newly replicated here or physical validation. Reproduce the full archived calculations and derive rates from material dynamics.

entries.title: Review 6.0 numerical checks and warnings
entries.summary: The forward script records 137 regression assertions. Three extreme elastic rows triggered quadrature warnings for small moment integrals; one selected refinement also warns.
entries.keywords: Methods The checks are not experiments; warned rows are illustrative, not precision-certified. Retain warnings, reproduce the source archive, test nonperturbative limits.

entries.title: Gravitational versus electromagnetic timing
entries.summary: Review 6.0 quotes the published GW170817/GRB 170817A differential speed constraint of approximately −3 × 10⁻¹⁵ to +7 × 10⁻¹⁶.
entries.keywords: Fields Depends on emission-time and propagation assumptions; not a direct isotropic coordinate-speed bound. Predict arrival lags with source, detector, clock and field parameters.

entries.title: Unified observational completion

entries.keywords: Methods Passing restricted numerical controls does not establish an alternative cosmology. Use held-out shared-parameter optical, timing, geometric and clock tests.

entries.title: Light, energy and invariant mass
entries.summary: Light has measurable energy and momentum. A nonzero invariant photon rest mass is a separate hypothesis, not a consequence of radiation pressure or gravity.
entries.keywords: Maxwell electrodynamics and the standard photon describe zero invariant mass. A positive invariant mass would change the dispersion relation and can introduce additional polarization and electrostatic screening constraints. Review 6.0 §5.2 treats a positive frequency gap in a candidate sector. Here C and initial energy are normalized to one, so a gap fraction g yields group speed √(1−g²). A photon carrying energy is not proof of a positive gap. Compare dispersion, static electric forces, polarization and emission/receiver spectra using shared parameters. A bound on rest mass is not a detection.

entries.title: One progression, different clock readings
entries.summary: The proposed universal progression T is a research choice. Different measured clock counts must be explained; identical progression does not establish a detectable absolute clock.
entries.keywords: Special relativity predicts proper time along an inertial trajectory. Atomic clocks, particle lifetimes and gravitational time comparisons constrain any alternative account. ArcSecs uses T and a process rate ν(T); a candidate must derive each physical rate and reproduce the complete set of comparisons, not just choose a rate that fits one clock. Compare clock technologies and moving-particle lifetimes using the same specified physical rate law.

entries.title: Distinguishing energy loss from slowing
entries.summary: Energy, frequency and group speed are distinct. A fixed-gap drag model permits energy loss with very little speed change, and the zero-gap limit does not slow at all.
entries.keywords: Redshifts arise in standard physics from relative motion, gravitational conditions and cosmological evolution. Propagation in media can alter group speed; a spectral shift alone does not identify a mechanism. The fixed-gap momentum-loss control in the book is an explicitly phenomenological branch. Review 6.0 also studies conversion and energy transfer; a stationary loss law alone does not generate observed arrival stretching. Identify the energy recipient and test pulse stretching, image blur, spectral noise and independent timing.

entries.title: Time as event ordering
entries.summary: The charter treats When as a relation between events. That ontological choice must be distinguished from measured duration and relativistic proper time.
entries.keywords: In relativity, proper time is measurable along a worldline; coordinate times describe events in chosen frames. Neither requires a flowing material. The physical-first account models ordered source events, transport and receiver counts separately. A variable transit delay can change arrival intervals, but an identical delay cannot. Measure a series of pulses with calibrated endpoint clocks; vary transit conditions independently.

entries.title: Space as measurable relations
entries.summary: Relative position, separation and geometry are measurable. The choice not to call space a material does not remove geometric laws.
entries.keywords: Euclidean geometry is a useful local approximation; relativistic geometry predicts measured trajectories and timing in its domain. Coordinates themselves are not material objects. ArcSecs treats Where as relative arrangement. Physical states and interactions must give coordinate-independent predictions for actual rulers and other instruments. Repeat ranging with different reference origins and compare invariant separations in the declared measurement regime.

entries.title: Physical attributes and system mass
entries.summary: Physical states carry measurable energy and momentum, but energy-equivalent mass, invariant mass and geometric extent are distinct quantities.
entries.keywords: For a system, invariant mass is defined by total four-momentum. A field state need not have a rigid classical boundary or nonzero individual rest mass. The charter asks for a physical inventory. Its technical interpretation requires defining mass and extent operationally before proposing an invariant mass for every entity. This control uses the standard massless two-photon reference. Measure total energy and vector momentum of a closed system; distinguish the aggregate invariant from constituent invariant masses.

entries.title: Geometry versus a literal fabric
entries.summary: Relativistic geometry is a successful predictive framework. Rejecting a literal fabric metaphor does not reject measured proper times, trajectories or gravity.
entries.keywords: The standard inertial proper-time factor is √(1−β²). General relativity extends the predictions to gravity using a dynamical metric. The research seeks physical interaction laws that recover the same predictions and offer independently discriminating tests. The standard factor here is a comparator, not a proposed alternative mechanism. Compare precision clock measurements, orbital effects, gravitational waves and light deflection with a derived alternative law.

entries.title: Group speed and causal speed
entries.summary: A field characteristic may be faster than a slow massive packet without exceeding the local causal maximum. No controllable faster-than-light signal is demonstrated.
entries.keywords: In standard vacuum relativity c is the local causal speed. Group speed and front speed in dispersive media are distinct. A closing rate is not a local information speed. C-01 separates the emission ceiling, electromagnetic front, all-sector causal characteristic, packet group speed and separation rate. The research requires a derived ordering and physical signal protocol. Test actual signal fronts with independently synchronized endpoints and an explicitly stated causal theory.

entries.title: Closing and separation rates versus causality
entries.summary: Coordinate separation rates may exceed a local light-speed benchmark; this does not imply that one body or signal travels locally faster than c.
entries.keywords: Special relativity gives relative speed 2β/(1+β²) times c for opposite equal speeds in one inertial frame. Cosmological recession is a distinct large-scale quantity. Review 6.0 C-01 uses this two-spacecraft thought experiment to separate inherited motion and emission. It expressly does not demonstrate single-photon superluminal motion. Measure signal arrival and relative velocity with the appropriate clocks and frame transformations.

entries.title: Observable reach and total cosmic extent
entries.summary: A finite causal reach does not determine the total physical extent of the universe. The observable horizon is not necessarily a material wall.
entries.keywords: Cosmological particle horizons depend on the expansion history and differ from Hubble radius and event horizon. Observations constrain curvature and accessible structure, not every possible parent domain. ArcSecs considers the total cosmos separately from the observed domain. A real boundary or outside region would require a field/interface model and observational signature. Use independent observations of curvature, topology, sky signatures and causal histories; a domain boundary needs separate evidence.

entries.title: Modeled cosmic age and total history
entries.summary: The conventional cosmic age is an inference from a calibrated expansion history. The duration of all hypothetical physical reality is a different, unanswered question.
entries.keywords: A flat matter–Λ reference gives a calculable expansion age for specified H₀ and matter fraction. The full standard inference includes radiation, observational constraints and uncertainties. The research distinguishes an age inferred for our domain from an unknown parent history. It retains the hot Big Bang as a possible physical history and requires independent chronometers. Compare cosmic expansion fits with stellar and other physical age indicators, using the same model assumptions and uncertainties.

entries.title: When astronomical distances and sizes can change
entries.summary: Distance corrections are testable and can have either sign. The charter’s smaller-and-closer premise must not become an assumed correction for every object.
entries.keywords: Geometric anchors, calibrated candles, rulers, spectroscopy and time intervals give complementary constraints. A reclassified foreground object does not invalidate the distances of spectroscopically confirmed galaxies. ArcSecs calls for geometric-first audits and joint fits, with positive and negative controls. This lesson isolates an unmodeled extinction term and a calibrated distance. Compare geometric anchors, extinction, flux, angles, spectra and arrival intervals with shared parameters and held-out observations.

entries.title: Invariant mass
entries.summary: Mass defined by the total energy–momentum invariant, not simply energy divided by c².

entries.title: Group speed
entries.summary: Rate of propagation of a wave-packet envelope in a specified dispersion law. Distinct from signal-front speed.

entries.title: Proper time
entries.summary: Time measured by an ideal clock along its worldline in relativity.

entries.title: Universal progression T
entries.summary: Proposed common evolution parameter; not an experimentally established absolute clock.

entries.title: Causal front
entries.summary: Leading boundary of a causal disturbance in a specified theory, not necessarily the group speed.

entries.title: Separation rate
entries.summary: Rate of change of distance under a specified coordinate convention; not automatically a local relative speed.

entries.title: Observable horizon
entries.summary: Limit of causal accessibility determined by the assumed cosmic history, not necessarily a physical wall.

entries.title: Hubble constant
entries.summary: Present expansion-rate parameter in a conventional cosmological model.

entries.title: Distance bias
entries.summary: Difference between an inferred and calibrated distance under declared assumptions. It can have either sign.

entries.title: Negative control
entries.summary: Specified model condition expected to remove an effect or reveal a failure; passing it is not empirical validation.

entries.title: Luz, energía y masa invariante
entries.summary: La luz transporta energía y momento medibles. Una masa invariante no nula del fotón es una hipótesis distinta, no una consecuencia de la presión de radiación ni de la gravedad.
entries.keywords: La electrodinámica estándar describe fotones sin masa invariante. El modelo con brecha de energía en Review 6.0 §5.2 propone una relación de dispersión diferente; no deriva el origen de la brecha. Comparar dispersión, fuerzas electrostáticas, polarización y espectros de emisión y recepción con parámetros compartidos. Una cota de masa no es una detección.

entries.title: Una progresión, distintas lecturas de reloj
entries.summary: La progresión universal T es una elección de modelo. Las diferencias observadas entre relojes requieren una explicación; no establecen un reloj absoluto detectable.
entries.keywords: La relatividad especial predice el tiempo propio. ArcSecs propone tasas de procesos ν(T); deben derivarse y reproducir todas las comparaciones, no ajustarse a un solo reloj. Comparar tecnologías de reloj y vidas medias de partículas en movimiento mediante una misma ley física de tasas.

entries.title: Energía y velocidad durante la propagación
entries.summary: Energía, frecuencia y velocidad de grupo son distintas. En el modelo de arrastre con brecha fija puede perderse energía con un cambio de velocidad muy pequeño; sin brecha no disminuye la velocidad.
entries.keywords: El corrimiento al rojo estándar puede deberse al movimiento, la gravedad o la expansión. El arrastre propuesto es fenomenológico; por sí solo no reproduce el estiramiento de los intervalos de llegada. Identificar el receptor de energía y medir estiramiento de pulsos, desenfoque, ruido espectral y tiempos independientes.

entries.title: El cuándo: eventos y llegada de pulsos
entries.summary: La carta considera el cuándo una relación entre eventos. Esta elección ontológica no equivale a negar las duraciones medidas ni el tiempo propio relativista.
entries.keywords: La relatividad distingue tiempo propio y coordenadas temporales. El enfoque físico separa emisión, transporte y recepción: un retardo constante no modifica los intervalos de llegada. Medir una serie de pulsos con relojes calibrados en los extremos y variar las condiciones de tránsito independientemente.

entries.title: El dónde: posición relativa y geometría
entries.summary: La posición relativa, la separación y la geometría son medibles. No considerar el espacio una sustancia no elimina las leyes geométricas.
entries.keywords: La geometría euclidiana aproxima situaciones locales; la geometría relativista predice trayectorias y tiempos. ArcSecs exige que las interacciones den predicciones independientes del origen de coordenadas. Repetir mediciones de distancia usando diferentes orígenes y comparar separaciones invariantes en el régimen declarado.

entries.title: Existencia física y masa de un sistema
entries.summary: La energía y el momento son medibles. La masa equivalente de energía, la masa invariante y la extensión geométrica son conceptos diferentes.
entries.keywords: La masa invariante de un sistema se define por su cuadrimomento total. Este control usa dos fotones estándar sin masa; su sistema puede tener masa invariante positiva sin que cada fotón la tenga. Medir energía total y momento vectorial de un sistema cerrado; distinguir el invariante agregado de los invariantes individuales.

entries.title: Geometría y sustancia física
entries.summary: La geometría relativista tiene éxito predictivo. Rechazar una metáfora de tejido literal no invalida los tiempos propios, las trayectorias o la gravedad medidos.
entries.keywords: La relatividad especial predice √(1−β²) como factor inercial de tiempo propio. La relatividad general emplea una métrica dinámica. El programa busca leyes de interacción que recuperen esas predicciones y permitan pruebas discriminantes. Comparar relojes de precisión, órbitas, ondas gravitacionales y desviación de la luz con una ley alternativa derivada.

entries.title: Velocidad de grupo y causalidad
entries.summary: Una característica de campo puede superar la velocidad de un paquete lento sin superar el límite causal local. No se demuestra ninguna señal controlable más rápida que la luz.
entries.keywords: En la relatividad estándar en el vacío, c es la velocidad causal local. El proyecto C-01 distingue techo de emisión, frente electromagnético, características causales, velocidad de grupo y tasa de separación. Medir frentes de señal con extremos sincronizados de forma independiente y una teoría causal explícita.

entries.title: Separación de objetos y velocidad local
entries.summary: Una tasa de separación en coordenadas puede superar c sin que un cuerpo o una señal lo haga localmente.
entries.keywords: Para velocidades opuestas iguales βc en un marco inercial, la velocidad relativa relativista es 2βc/(1+β²). El ejemplo de dos naves de C-01 distingue la separación de la propagación de una señal. Medir llegada de señales y velocidad relativa con relojes adecuados y transformaciones de marco.

entries.title: Horizonte y extensión del cosmos
entries.summary: Un alcance causal finito no determina la extensión total. El horizonte observable no es necesariamente una pared material.
entries.keywords: Los horizontes cosmológicos dependen de la expansión y no son idénticos al radio de Hubble. ArcSecs distingue el dominio observado de un cosmos total hipotético; una frontera real requiere su propio mecanismo y señal observacional. Contrastar curvatura, topología, firmas del cielo e historias causales independientes.

entries.title: Edad cosmológica e historia total
entries.summary: La edad cosmológica convencional se infiere de una historia de expansión calibrada. La duración de toda realidad física hipotética es otra cuestión.
entries.keywords: Una referencia plana de materia y Λ permite calcular una edad con H₀ y fracción de materia. ArcSecs conserva el Big Bang caliente como historia posible y distingue la historia del dominio de una historia anterior desconocida. Comparar ajustes de expansión con edades estelares y otros cronómetros independientes, incluyendo incertidumbres.

entries.title: Distancias y tamaños astronómicos
entries.summary: Las correcciones de distancia pueden tener ambos signos. La premisa de objetos más pequeños y cercanos no es una corrección universal establecida.
entries.keywords: Anclas geométricas, luminosidades calibradas, reglas, espectros e intervalos temporales aportan restricciones complementarias. Este control aísla un sesgo de magnitud respecto a una distancia calibrada. Contrastar anclas geométricas, extinción, flujo, ángulos, espectros e intervalos con parámetros comunes y datos reservados.

entries.title: Masa invariante
entries.summary: Masa definida por el invariante de energía y momento totales, no simplemente energía dividida por c².

entries.title: Velocidad de grupo
entries.summary: Velocidad de propagación de la envolvente de un paquete de ondas en una relación de dispersión dada. Distinta de la velocidad del frente.

entries.title: Tiempo propio
entries.summary: Tiempo medido por un reloj ideal a lo largo de su línea de universo en relatividad.

entries.title: Progresión universal T
entries.summary: Parámetro común de evolución propuesto; no es un reloj absoluto establecido experimentalmente.

entries.title: Frente causal
entries.summary: Límite delantero de una perturbación causal en una teoría dada, no necesariamente la velocidad de grupo.

entries.title: Tasa de separación
entries.summary: Variación de distancia por unidad de tiempo según una convención de coordenadas; no equivale necesariamente a una velocidad relativa local.

entries.title: Horizonte observable
entries.summary: Límite de accesibilidad causal determinado por la historia cósmica supuesta, no necesariamente una pared física.

entries.title: Constante de Hubble
entries.summary: Parámetro de la tasa de expansión actual en un modelo cosmológico convencional.

entries.title: Sesgo de distancia
entries.summary: Diferencia entre una distancia inferida y otra calibrada bajo supuestos declarados. Puede tener ambos signos.

entries.title: Control negativo
entries.summary: Condición especificada del modelo que debe eliminar un efecto o revelar un fallo; superarlo no es una validación empírica.

entries.title: Lumière, énergie et masse invariante
entries.summary: La lumière transporte une énergie et une quantité de mouvement mesurables. Une masse invariante non nulle du photon constitue une hypothèse distincte, non une conséquence de la pression de radiation ou de la gravité.
entries.keywords: L’électrodynamique standard décrit des photons de masse invariante nulle. Le modèle à seuil énergétique de Review 6.0 §5.2 modifie la dispersion sans dériver l’origine du seuil. Comparer dispersion, forces électrostatiques, polarisation et spectres d’émission et de réception avec des paramètres communs. Une borne de masse n’est pas une détection.

entries.title: Une progression, des horloges différentes
entries.summary: La progression universelle T est un choix de modèle. Les différences de comptage des horloges demandent une explication, mais ne prouvent pas une horloge absolue détectable.
entries.keywords: La relativité restreinte prédit le temps propre. ArcSecs propose des taux de processus ν(T) ; il faut les dériver et reproduire toutes les comparaisons, pas seulement ajuster une horloge. Comparer différentes technologies d’horloge et durées de vie de particules en mouvement avec une même loi physique.

entries.title: Énergie et vitesse pendant la propagation
entries.summary: Énergie, fréquence et vitesse de groupe sont distinctes. Un freinage à seuil fixe peut faire perdre de l’énergie avec très peu de variation de vitesse ; sans seuil, la vitesse reste constante.
entries.keywords: Les décalages spectraux standards proviennent notamment du mouvement, de la gravité et de l’expansion. Le freinage proposé est phénoménologique et ne suffit pas à reproduire l’étirement des intervalles d’arrivée. Identifier le récepteur de l’énergie et tester étirement des impulsions, flou, bruit spectral et chronométrage indépendant.

entries.title: Le quand : événements et arrivée des impulsions
entries.summary: La charte traite le quand comme une relation entre événements. Ce choix ontologique se distingue des durées mesurées et du temps propre relativiste.
entries.keywords: La relativité distingue temps propre et coordonnées temporelles. L’approche physique sépare émission, transport et réception : un retard constant ne change pas les intervalles d’arrivée. Mesurer des impulsions avec des horloges calibrées aux extrémités et faire varier indépendamment le transport.

entries.title: Le où : position relative et géométrie
entries.summary: Position relative, séparation et géométrie sont mesurables. Ne pas considérer l’espace comme une substance ne supprime pas les lois géométriques.
entries.keywords: La géométrie euclidienne est une approximation locale ; la géométrie relativiste prédit les trajectoires et les durées. ArcSecs exige des prédictions indépendantes du choix de l’origine. Répéter les mesures de distance avec différentes origines et comparer les séparations invariantes dans le régime déclaré.

entries.title: Existence physique et masse d’un système
entries.summary: Énergie et quantité de mouvement sont mesurables. Masse équivalente énergétique, masse invariante et extension géométrique sont des notions distinctes.
entries.keywords: La masse invariante d’un système est définie par son quadrivecteur énergie-impulsion total. Deux photons standards sans masse peuvent former un système de masse invariante positive. Mesurer énergie totale et quantité de mouvement vectorielle d’un système fermé ; distinguer invariant global et invariants individuels.

entries.title: Géométrie et substance physique
entries.summary: La géométrie relativiste est un cadre prédictif efficace. Rejeter la métaphore d’un tissu matériel ne réfute pas les temps propres, les trajectoires ou la gravité mesurés.
entries.keywords: La relativité restreinte donne le facteur inertiel √(1−β²). La relativité générale utilise une métrique dynamique. Le programme cherche des lois d’interaction reproduisant ces prédictions et offrant des tests discriminants. Comparer horloges de précision, orbites, ondes gravitationnelles et déviation de la lumière avec une loi alternative dérivée.

entries.title: Vitesse de groupe et causalité
entries.summary: Une caractéristique de champ peut être plus rapide qu’un paquet lent sans dépasser la limite causale locale. Aucun signal supraluminique contrôlable n’est démontré.
entries.keywords: Dans la relativité standard dans le vide, c est la vitesse causale locale. C-01 distingue plafond d’émission, front électromagnétique, caractéristiques causales, vitesse de groupe et taux de séparation. Mesurer les fronts de signal avec des extrémités synchronisées indépendamment et une théorie causale explicite.

entries.title: Séparation des objets et vitesse locale
entries.summary: Un taux de séparation en coordonnées peut dépasser c sans qu’un corps ou un signal dépasse localement c.
entries.keywords: Pour des vitesses opposées égales βc dans un référentiel inertiel, la vitesse relative relativiste vaut 2βc/(1+β²). L’expérience de pensée C-01 des deux vaisseaux distingue séparation et propagation d’un signal. Mesurer l’arrivée des signaux et la vitesse relative avec les horloges et transformations de référentiel appropriées.

entries.title: Horizon et étendue du cosmos
entries.summary: Une portée causale finie ne détermine pas l’étendue physique totale. L’horizon observable n’est pas nécessairement une paroi matérielle.
entries.keywords: Les horizons cosmologiques dépendent de l’expansion et se distinguent du rayon de Hubble. ArcSecs distingue le domaine observé d’un cosmos total hypothétique ; une frontière réelle exige un mécanisme et une signature propres. Confronter courbure, topologie, signatures du ciel et histoires causales indépendantes.

entries.title: Âge cosmologique et histoire totale
entries.summary: L’âge cosmologique conventionnel est inféré d’une histoire d’expansion calibrée. La durée de toute réalité physique hypothétique est une autre question.
entries.keywords: Une référence plate matière–Λ donne un âge à partir de H₀ et de la fraction de matière. ArcSecs conserve le Big Bang chaud comme histoire possible et distingue celle du domaine d’une éventuelle histoire antérieure. Comparer ajustements d’expansion, âges stellaires et autres chronomètres indépendants, avec leurs incertitudes.

entries.title: Distances et tailles astronomiques
entries.summary: Les corrections de distance peuvent être de l’un ou l’autre signe. La prémisse « plus petits et plus proches » n’est pas une correction universelle établie.
entries.keywords: Ancrages géométriques, luminosités calibrées, règles, spectres et intervalles temporels apportent des contraintes complémentaires. Ce contrôle isole un biais de magnitude par rapport à une distance calibrée. Confronter ancrages géométriques, extinction, flux, angles, spectres et intervalles avec des paramètres communs et des données réservées.

entries.title: Masse invariante
entries.summary: Masse définie par l’invariant énergie-impulsion total, et non simplement par l’énergie divisée par c².

entries.title: Vitesse de groupe
entries.summary: Vitesse de propagation de l’enveloppe d’un paquet d’ondes pour une dispersion donnée. Distincte de la vitesse du front.

entries.title: Temps propre
entries.summary: Temps mesuré par une horloge idéale le long de sa ligne d’univers en relativité.

entries.title: Progression universelle T
entries.summary: Paramètre commun d’évolution proposé ; pas une horloge absolue établie expérimentalement.

entries.title: Front causal
entries.summary: Limite avant d’une perturbation causale dans une théorie donnée, distincte en général de la vitesse de groupe.

entries.title: Taux de séparation
entries.summary: Variation de distance par unité de temps selon une convention de coordonnées ; pas nécessairement une vitesse relative locale.

entries.title: Horizon observable
entries.summary: Limite d’accessibilité causale déterminée par l’histoire cosmique supposée, pas nécessairement une paroi physique.

entries.title: Constante de Hubble
entries.summary: Paramètre du taux d’expansion actuel dans un modèle cosmologique conventionnel.

entries.title: Biais de distance
entries.summary: Différence entre une distance inférée et une distance calibrée sous des hypothèses déclarées. Peut être de signe positif ou négatif.

entries.title: Contrôle négatif
entries.summary: Condition spécifiée du modèle censée supprimer un effet ou révéler un échec ; la réussir ne constitue pas une validation empirique.

entries.title: Journey of a photon
entries.summary: Watch the conditional fixed-gap packet and the zero-gap reference move along a shared normalized path.
entries.keywords: Does energy loss necessarily imply significant slowing? The path length is the trapezoidal integral of returned group-speed samples divided by C times the modeled duration. The path is not an astronomical distance; the marker at its right end is a reference, not a modeled detector.

entries.title: Three clocks, one coordinate interval
entries.summary: Watch reference, candidate and special-relativistic clock counts accumulate on one time axis.
entries.keywords: Can one stipulated clock-rate ratio match all relativistic predictions? Each revolution represents one count, not a mechanism inside an actual atomic clock. The candidate rate is stipulated; matching a single relative velocity is not independent validation.

entries.title: Separation is not signal speed
entries.summary: Move along the speed-parameter sweep and compare separation rate with relativistic relative speed.
entries.keywords: How can common-frame separation exceed C without superluminal local signals? The arrows represent each ship’s speed in the common reference frame, not a trajectory or a signal. The displayed relative speed follows the existing special-relativistic calculation.

entries.title: Observable reach and hypothetical cosmic domains
entries.summary: Compare an illustrative spherical domain with the region accessible to the assumed signal reach.
entries.keywords: Does an observable reach establish the total size of the cosmos? Nested circles show a central cross-section of the assumed spheres; the accessible fraction is a volume ratio, not an area ratio. This is not wall dynamics, a cosmological horizon calculation or evidence for a neighboring universe.

entries.title: Age of a reference expansion model
entries.summary: Compare two flat matter–Λ reference age curves over the same Hubble constant range.
entries.keywords: How do Hubble constant and matter fraction change the modeled age? This is a parameter sweep of a flat matter-plus-Λ age formula, neglecting radiation. It is not an animation of cosmic expansion, a fit to measurements, or the age of a hypothetical parent cosmos. The reference matter fraction is an illustrative comparison value.

entries.title: Coherent conversion and escape
entries.summary: Observe the incident, local-converted and escaped populations with the reversible zero-escape reference.
entries.keywords: When does total converted population remain monotone? The segmented reservoir is a population ledger for the selected-mode solution, not a spatial or individual-photon trajectory. Display geometry clips tiny negative floating-point residuals to zero; raw readouts and exports preserve them.

entries.title: Can a fixed-gap wall be traversed?
entries.summary: Inspect retention bounds along the ceiling-ratio sweep and the two selected-case drag limits.
entries.keywords: Can the two necessary constant-drag requirements overlap? The curve is log₁₀ of the maximum retained energy fraction. The two selected-case drag limits are separate from the scrubbed sample. A finite interval is necessary, not proof of a physical wall or a complete traversal solution.

entries.title: From light attenuation to distance bias
entries.summary: Compare calibrated and inferred distance on a shared spatial scale as the attenuation parameter changes.
entries.keywords: Can an unmodeled attenuation change inferred distance in either direction? The two rays represent distance estimates for the same object, not two objects or a change in the actual distance. The signed attenuation experiment is conditional; it does not establish a universal distance correction.

entries.title: Geometric distance anchors
entries.summary: Compare LMC and NGC 4258 shift-to-uncertainty ratios along a common percentage axis.
entries.keywords: How large is a proposed shift relative to quoted anchor uncertainties? The bars are magnitudes relative to the combined quoted uncertainties under unchanged calibration. They are not independent Gaussian detection significances, likelihoods or new measurements.

entries.title: Does a positive gap reduce modeled group speed?
entries.summary: Can momentum loss at fixed propagation time discriminate zero-gap and positive-gap conditional histories?
entries.keywords: A positive rest-energy gap reduces final modeled group speed at fixed drag and duration. Zero-gap energy loss need not change group speed. An observed spectral shift alone cannot distinguish mechanisms.

entries.title: Does escape increase the final escaped population?
entries.summary: Does the Markov escape term permit net escape in this selected-mode model?
entries.keywords: At the chosen interaction duration, nonzero escape gives a greater escaped population than the closed reference. Coherent closed conversion can oscillate without any escaped population. This endpoint does not test continuous individual photon slowing.

entries.title: Does fixed transit delay preserve pulse spacing?
entries.summary: Can a change of emitted spacing be distinguished from a constant transit delay?
entries.keywords: Increasing the emission interval increases the received interval by the same amount in the specified stationary-delay model. A constant delay shifts arrivals without stretching intervals. Moving endpoints or a time-varying channel require separate modeling.

entries.title: Does ignored attenuation bias inferred size?
entries.summary: How does a signed unmodeled magnitude offset affect inferred/calibrated size?
entries.keywords: Positive attenuation ignored by the model increases the inferred/calibrated ratio. No offset leaves that ratio at one; real astronomical calibration can involve additional variables.

entries.title: Does a common translation preserve physical separation?
entries.summary: Which changes affect Euclidean separation in the teaching model?
entries.keywords: Increasing horizontal separation at fixed vertical separation increases the invariant separation. A common coordinate translation changes coordinate labels without changing the separation; this does not establish a new theory of geometry.
